title: Pattern library for customer-specific Terraform overlays and upgrade-safe module composition for VPC/private deployments
creator: Diego Rivera
description: Goal: define and implement a repeatable, audit-friendly pattern for customer-specific Terraform customizations for Private (VPC) deployments. Focus areas: overlay composition strategies, variable/inputs conventions, module wrapper patterns to enable safe runtime upgrades, CI gating and automated health checks that validate upgrades and drift, and migration guidance for existing customers. Deliverables include a pattern library, example repo(s), CI templates, and documentation for Solutions/SEs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Pattern doc published in the internal infra handbook and linked from onboarding playbook. 2) Example repo with 3 overlay strategies (module composition, Terragrunt layer, and directory-per-customer workspace) that can deploy a minimal VPC + Redwood Private control plane in a sandbox. 3) CI pipeline template that runs plan, apply-to-canary, health-checks, and auto-rollback on failure. 4) Security checklist completed and approval obtained. 5) At least one pilot customer migrated to the recommended pattern without production downtime.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Research and shortlist patterns (1w). Phase 2: Prototype three example implementations in a shared sandbox (2w). Phase 3: Build CI templates + health-check scripts and a terragrunt wrapper for the most promising pattern (2w). Phase 4: Document migration steps, run pilot migration with SE (1w). Phase 5: Capture learnings, finalize pattern, and propose as default for new Private customers.
technical_decisions: 1) Prefer module-wrapper pattern (thin composition module that pins public module inputs and exposes a stable facade) for upgrade safety because it isolates internal schema changes. 2) Recommend Terragrunt for teams that need heavy per-customer overlays with minimal duplication; recommend pure TF module composition for simple customers to avoid Terragrunt lock-in. 3) Use terraform state separation per-customer (per-tenant state files) and avoid shared workspaces to limit blast radius. 4) Enforce semantic versioning on infra modules and keep migration notes in CHANGELOG.md. 5) CI should run 'terraform plan' against both current and target module versions and run automated health checks in a sandbox before rollouts.
recommended_variable_conventions: - customer_id: string (slug) - env: string (dev|staging|prod) - network_cidr: string - azs: list - public_subnets: list - private_subnets: list - kms_key_id: string (optional) - monitoring_endpoint: string - enable_bastion: bool - allowed_ip_ranges: list - upgrade_channel: string (canary|stable) - overlay_profile: string (minimal|standard|enterprise)
overlay_patterns_explained: 1) Module-wrapper (recommended): Create a thin wrapper module per customer that calls upstream redwood/private modules. Wrapper pins inputs, adds customer policies (tags, KMS), and exposes a stable interface to SEs. Pros: clear upgrade path, local migration control. Cons: some code duplication. 2) Terragrunt overlays: Use Terragrunt live folders per customer with inherited common.hcl config. Pros: concise per-customer overrides, easy secrets interpolation. Cons: Terragrunt is an extra tool and couples customers to the wrapper. 3) Directory-per-customer workspaces: Separate terraform directories for each customer. Pros: explicit per-customer state and config. Cons: harder to share logic and keep modules synchronized.
upgrade_strategy: - Use semantic versions on modules and a release branch for infra changes. - CI runs a 'dry-run' plan with the new module pinned and stores the plan artifact. - Execute canary apply in sandbox or a designated 'canary' customer environment. - Run automated health checks (connectivity, control-plane API smoke tests, KV cache warm-up, and sample inference traffic). - If health-checks pass, schedule staged rollout across customers grouped by risk. - Provide clear rollback plans: terraform apply to previous module version + run health-checks. - Maintain a migration shim in wrappers for breaking schema changes (translation layer).
health_checks_and_validation: Smoke checks implemented as standalone scripts invoked by CI: 1) infra-health.sh: verifies VPC, route tables, subnets exist and respond. 2) controlplane-smoke: confirms Redwood Private control plane endpoints register and respond to /health. 3) sample-infer: sends a low-cost inference request to the instance to ensure end-to-end path. 4) drift-detect: run 'terraform plan' after apply and fail if changes are detected. Health-checks return structured exit codes; CI interprets non-zero as failure and triggers rollback.
examples_and_artifacts: - Repo: github.com/redwood-inference/priv-vpc-patterns (prototype branches: module-wrapper, terragrunt-overlay, per-customer-dir). - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/priv-vpc-patterns/pull/12 (module-wrapper prototype). - Sandbox deploy run: https://ci.redwood-infra/sandbox-runs/459. - Demo runbook: docs/internal/private-overlays-runbook.md
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customer customization sprawl leads to unmaintainable forks. Mitigation: mandate a small approved overlay surface and use wrapper modules with clear allowed extensions. Risk: Upgrades cause downtime. Mitigation: canary apply + automated health checks + mandatory rollback playbook. Risk: Terragrunt lock-in. Mitigation: support both patterns and provide migration scripts to unwrap Terragrunt into native TF when needed.
followups_and_next_steps: - Create SE-facing migration checklist and one-pager (owner: Maya). - Implement policy-as-code checks (OPA) to enforce allowed overlay inputs (owner: Security Infra). - Pilot migration with customer 'Acme Health' and capture telemetry (owner: Solutions Eng). - Add automated tag validation hook in CI to ensure release notes and changelog entries accompany module bumps.
